readrole_instructions:
Read the materials below. While you do, try to get into character—figure out: what matters to you? And what would you like to get from this negotiation?

Take notes on the right to help you prepare. You can use those notes when the negotiation starts.
Try the scoring calculator to see what different offers would be worth to you.

roles.narrative:
You are an ambitious job Candidate negotiating a sales role with a young company. You care about income, but money isn't all that matters in life. You want room to build a career, protect time with your family, and avoid getting stuck in a role where your work is visible but you are not developing professionally. Your objective is to reach an agreement with the highest total score you can, while recognizing that the Recruiter has priorities of their own that may conflict with yours. You prefer a higher salary and budget and an earlier start. Starting promptly would help restore your income and career momentum, while a long delay would be substantially more disruptive. Salary and personal work-expense budget may be any non-negative amount. The figures below are scoring reference points, not limits on what you may propose. • Annual salary: $35,000 gives you −2 points,
$50,000 gives you 0, and $65,000 gives you +2. • Starting date: January 1 gives you +1 point, March 1 gives you 0, May 1 gives you −1, July 1 gives you −2, and dates in September give you −3. Dates between these examples receive proportional points. A start after September means the deal cannot go ahead. • The personal budget: $5,000 gives you −2,
$10,000 gives you 0, and $15,000 gives you +2. Salary and budget amounts between these reference points receive intermediate scores. Amounts outside them continue to gain or lose points at the same rate. For example, a $7,000 budget is worth about −1.2 points to you. You do not need to calculate this yourself. These headline contract terms are easy to put numbers on. However, the interview also left you thinking about what the job would actually be like and what other terms you might ask for given what matters to you. **Background Information** On the way home, you think about the company's usual 30 vacation days per year and 3 remote-working days per week. Those arrangements seem reasonable. Each is worth 0 points to you. Still, more flexibility would mean more time with your family and more room for interests and professional development outside work, while less flexibility would work against those interests. • For vacation, 10 days per year are worth −1 point to you and 50 days are worth +1. • For remote work, 1 day per week is worth −1 and all 5 working days are worth +1. The two features are scored separately. Values between or beyond these examples continue at the same rate; vacation cannot exceed 365 days per year, and remote work cannot exceed the five working days per week. You also remember the Recruiter's stories about how people grow in the company. • One new hire attended an external professional training program; another was paired with an experienced mentor. • Someone else built relationships with senior colleagues after volunteering at a recruitment fair. Those examples appealed to you because they offered concrete ways to learn and build relationships rather than vague promises of “growth.” Other stories were less appealing. • The Recruiter joked that sociable employees often end up organizing team events. • The company regularly shares strong client stories on social media. Employees close to those accounts may be asked to help shape the posts, and confident employees sometimes present at conferences. … You enjoy people, but you do not want every spare hour turned into company visibility. A recruitment fair might expand your network; recurring publicity work might simply expand your workload. That evening, your spouse asked whether the company would support the professional association that has helped you and what would happen if you eventually wanted to leave. • Sponsored membership could help keep your skills and outside relationships alive. • The question about leaving brought you back to the non-compete clause you had raised. • You want to show commitment without unnecessarily limiting your future. The interview also touched on everyday work resources, spending support, health and wellbeing benefits, and how people are evaluated and rewarded as their responsibilities grow. Some details may simply be background; others could become useful terms if you connect them to what matters to you. **Your score** is private and **translates** directly into the **bonus payment you** can **earn** from this task. Without a deal, you will continue your job search; you do not have another offer in hand. This fallback is worth 0 points.

tips:
Please answer using the role materials you have just read. When a question asks you to write an offer, describe that offer in your own words as carefully as you can. To review the role materials, press the button above.

Bonus Prolific payment: Among participants who pass our effort-screening test, 20% will be selected at random to receive a bonus that doubles their total payment for this task. We aim to pay this within 2 to 7 days after the study ends.

Tips on Negotiation

Get into character and think about what your first couple of offers would be, based on what matters to you and what you anticipate from your counterpart. When making offers remember the following:

  1. Include the three required features: salary, a personal work-expense budget and a starting date. Write your offer in your own words.
  2. Calculate, check, then submit. The platform calculates points automatically using rules set by the researchers. Check that it understood your offer before sending it.
  3. You may introduce other plausible job or contract features. Each additional feature is normally worth between −1 and +1 points to you, depending on your interests. The other party may value it differently.
  4. Some features may not fit the situation and will be worth 0 points. That doesn’t mean you should hold back on creative and thoughtful ideas!
  5. Both parties must officially accept the same offer, worth more than 0 points to each. Without an agreement, both receive 0 points.
